title: 含线路阻抗的对称 Y–Y 电路：归结为一相
statement: 对称三相电源（正序，U̇_A = 220∠0° V）经三根端线向对称星形负载供电，没有中线。每根端线的阻抗 Z_l = 1 + j1 Ω，每相负载 Z = 5 + j7 Ω。
求线电流 I_A、负载相电压 U_A'N' 和负载端线电压 U_A'B'（均为有效值）。

questions.ask: 负载相电压有效值 U_A'N' = ?
questions.explain: U_A'N' = I_A·|Z| = 22 × √(5² + 7²) = 22 × 8.602 ≈ 189.25 V，比电源相电压低，因为线路阻抗上有压降。

questions.ask: 负载端线电压有效值 U_A'B' = ?
没有中线，为什么还可以把 N' 与 N 短接、只算 A 相？
choices: 对称时由结点电压法 U̇_N'N = (U̇_A + U̇_B + U̇_C)/(3(Z_l + Z)) = 0，N' 与 N 等电位，短接不改变任何电流
因为 N' 点实际上接地了
这是一种近似，只有线路阻抗很小时才成立
因为 A 相电流最大，只需要算 A 相
questions.explain: 以 N 为参考点列 N' 的结点方程，三相电压之和为零，所以 U̇_N'N = 0。等电位的两点之间接一根导线不会有电流，于是可以“加上”一根理想中线，三相各自独立，只算一相即可。

hints: 先说明 U̇_N'N = 0，然后画出 A 相的单相电路：U̇_A、Z_l、Z 串联。
I_A = U_A / |Z_l + Z|，负载相电压 = I_A·|Z|。
负载端的三个相电压仍然对称，所以线电压是相电压的 √3 倍。
solution: **1. 中性点电压。** 以 N 为参考，对 N' 列结点方程：U̇_N'N·3/(Z_l + Z) = (U̇_A + U̇_B + U̇_C)/(Z_l + Z) = 0，所以 U̇_N'N = 0。

en.title: Balanced Y–Y with line impedance: the per-phase equivalent
statement: A balanced three-phase source (positive sequence, U̇_A = 220∠0° V) feeds a balanced wye load through three lines, with no neutral wire. Each line has impedance Z_l = 1 + j1 Ω and each load phase is Z = 5 + j7 Ω.
Find the line current I_A, the load phase voltage U_A'N' and the line voltage at the load U_A'B' (all rms).

questions.explain: Per-phase circuit: U̇_A across Z_l + Z = 6 + j8 = 10∠53.13° Ω, so I_A = 220/10 = 22 A.
U_A'N' = I_A·|Z| = 22 × √(5² + 7²) = 22 × 8.602 ≈ 189.25 V, lower than the source phase voltage because of the drop across the line.

questions.ask: rms line voltage at the load U_A'B' = ?
questions.explain: The load voltages are still balanced, so U_A'B' = √3 × U_A'N' = √3 × 189.25 ≈ 327.79 V.

questions.ask: There is no neutral wire. Why may we still join N' to N and solve phase A alone?
choices: In a balanced circuit nodal analysis gives U̇_N'N = (U̇_A + U̇_B + U̇_C)/(3(Z_l + Z)) = 0, so N' and N are at the same potential and joining them changes no current
It is an approximation that only holds when the line impedance is small
Because phase A has the largest current, only phase A needs solving
questions.explain: With N as reference, the node equation at N' contains the sum of the three phase voltages, which is zero, so U̇_N'N = 0. A wire between two points at equal potential carries no current, so an ideal neutral can be “added”; the three phases become independent and one of them suffices.

hints: First show that U̇_N'N = 0, then draw the phase-A circuit: U̇_A, Z_l and Z in series.
I_A = U_A / |Z_l + Z|, and the load phase voltage is I_A·|Z|.
The three load phase voltages are still balanced, so the line voltage is √3 times the phase voltage.
solution: **1. Neutral-point voltage.** With N as reference, the node equation at N' reads U̇_N'N·3/(Z_l + Z) = (U̇_A + U̇_B + U̇_C)/(Z_l + Z) = 0, so U̇_N'N = 0.
Check: each line loses I²·1 = 484 W, each load phase absorbs I²·5 = 2420 W, and each source phase delivers U·I·cos53.13° = 220 × 22 × 0.6 = 2904 W = 484 + 2420.
